target: Varken han eller hon kom.
english: Neither he nor she came.
tip: Varken ... eller is the fixed pair for neither ... nor: varken han eller hon. Use eller here, never och.

target: Det kommer att regna ikväll.
english: It is going to rain tonight.
tip: "Kommer att" + infinitive expresses predictions, especially weather and external events.

target: Istället för att vänta agerade vi.
english: Instead of waiting, we acted.
tip: Istället för att takes an infinitive: istället för att vänta = instead of waiting, not instead of to wait.

target: Vi ska gifta oss i sommar.
english: We are getting married this summer.
tip: "Ska" for planned future events. "I sommar" means this/next summer.

target: Om jag var du skulle jag vänta.
english: If I were you I would wait.
tip: For hypotheticals Swedish uses the past tense: om jag var du means if I were you, literally if I was you.

target: Hon slutförde inte bara rapporten utan förberedde också presentationen.
english: Not only did she finish the report, but she also prepared the presentation.
tip: Inte bara ... utan också frames not only ... but also: inte bara rapporten utan också presentationen.

target: Jag har redan ätit.
english: I have already eaten.
tip: In the perfect tense an adverb like redan sits between har and the participle: har redan ätit, not har ätit redan.

target: De springande barnen skrattade.
english: The running children laughed.
tip: Participles don't inflect: springande works with any gender/number.

target: De har förlorat passet.
english: They have lost their passport.
tip: When the owner is clear from context, Swedish uses the definite instead of a possessive: har förlorat passet, not sitt pass.

target: Hej då, vi ses senare!
english: Goodbye, see you later!
tip: The -s on ses makes it reciprocal: vi ses means we see each other, the everyday way to say see you.

target: Så länge du är här är jag glad.
english: As long as you're here I'm happy.
tip: "Så länge" = as long as. Second clause inverts after fronted subclause.

target: Hon berättade för mig att hon var sjuk.
english: She told me that she was sick.
tip: berätta needs för before the listener: berättade för mig means told me. You cannot drop the för.

target: Jag har bott i Sverige i två år nu.
english: I have lived in Sweden for two years now.
tip: For a length of time Swedish uses i: bott i två år means lived for two years, not för.

target: Han klagade över att det var kallt.
english: He complained that it was cold.
tip: klaga takes över for what you complain about: klagade över att means complained that. The preposition is fixed.

target: Hon berättade glatt att hon äntligen hade fått det nya jobbet.
english: She happily told that she had finally gotten the new job.
tip: Reported speech uses past perfect (hade fått) when the original was past tense (fick).

target: Den stängda dörren hela tiden under sommaren.
english: The closed door all the time during summer.
tip: Unlike English, Swedish past participles inflect like adjectives: en stängd dörr, ett stängt hus, and den stängda dörren.

target: Den leende flickan vinkade.
english: The smiling girl waved.
tip: Present participles like leende (smiling) end in -ande or -ende and keep one form no matter the noun.

target: Tystnaden var nästan öronbedövande.
english: The silence was almost deafening.
tip: "Öronbedövande" = ear-deafening. Swedish builds vivid compounds: noun + participle.

target: Vi har just kommit hem.
english: We have just come home.
tip: Just here means just now. It sits between har and kommit to say something happened moments ago.

target: Jag ringer upp dig senare.
english: I'll call you back later.
tip: The particle upp reshapes the verb: ringa alone means to call, but ringer upp means to phone someone back.

target: Att veta vart vinden blåser.
english: To know which way the wind blows.
tip: Vart means where to, for direction. Var means where something sits. Vart vinden blåser asks which way.

target: Han sa åt mig att vänta.
english: He told me to wait.
tip: Säga åt någon att means tell someone to do something. The åt is required: sa åt mig att vänta.

target: De undrade vem som hade ringt.
english: They wondered who had called.
tip: When the question word is the subject, add som: vem som hade ringt, never vem hade ringt.

target: Det visade sig att han hade rätt.
english: It turned out that he was right.
tip: Swedish says ha rätt, literally have right, to mean be correct: han hade rätt, he was right.

target: De anställda på företaget.
english: The employees at the company.
tip: "Anställd" (employed) functions as both participle and noun.

target: Enligt honom var det en bra idé.
english: According to him, it was a good idea.
tip: Front an adverbial like Enligt honom and the verb comes next, before the subject: var det, not det var.

target: Kundservicen på den där butiken är under all kritik.
english: The customer service at that shop is beneath contempt.
tip: Under all kritik literally means below all criticism: something so bad it is beyond critiquing at all.

target: De uppmanade oss att lämna.
english: They urged us to leave.
tip: After uppmanade, put the object oss first, then att lämna. Pattern: urge someone att plus the verb.

target: Jag har valt den blå.
english: I have chosen the blue one.
tip: Swedish drops the noun after den plus adjective. Here den blå means the blue one, with no noun needed.

target: Det sägs att sommaren blir varm.
english: It's said the summer will be warm.
tip: "Det sägs att" = it is said that – impersonal reported speech.
